title: OT network
pageHelp: VLANs (IEEE 802.1Q), zones and conduits (IEC 62443-3-2), the devices and data paths of the assets of {{site}}, and their live status.
whoCanAct: Whoever manages the site documents its OT network.
addressInvalid: Use an IPv4 or IPv6 address (192.0.2.10, 2001:db8::10).

card.error: The OT network could not be loaded.

overview.title: Live status
overview.help: Online, offline or unknown – only from the checks linked to an asset or its devices; never online without a check saying so. An asset without any check is not watched.

live.notWatchedHint: No check is linked: nothing tells whether it is online.
live.title: Live status
live.help: Checks linked to the asset itself; its devices have their own. Offline wins, unknown is never shown as online.
live.noOwnChecks: No check is linked to the asset itself.
live.hiddenCheck: A check you may not see
live.nothingWatched: Nothing on this site is watched yet: link monitor checks or dataset freshness to an asset or device on its page (Live status → Checks).

reasons.degraded: The monitor is degraded – reachable, not well.
reasons.unknown: The monitor has no result yet.
reasons.maintenance: In maintenance – it says nothing now.
reasons.off: Off as planned – every check of the monitor agrees.
reasons.disabled: The monitor or check is turned off.
reasons.stale: The data is older than allowed.
reasons.no_data: Nothing is published under this key (yet).
reasons.no_row: The dataset has no row for it.
reasons.no_time: The time column has no readable time.
reasons.hidden: It counts towards the status; what it checks is not shown to you.

checks.title: Linked checks
checks.help: A monitor (or one of its checks: a Gatus endpoint, a Checkmk service, the MQTT silent-device check, Kafka …) or the freshness of a dataset.
checks.checkHelp: Empty: the status of the whole monitor.
checks.datasetHelp: The key a process publishes to, e.g. iot.last-values
checks.timeColumnHelp: The time of the last value; empty: when the dataset was written.
checks.maxAgeHelp: Older is offline; empty: the dataset’s own freshness.
checks.hidden: A check you may not see – it stays as it is. You may remove it.

vlan.title: VLANs
vlan.help: IEEE 802.1Q VLANs with their subnets and address ranges. A VLAN can name the Steward network segment it is – nothing becomes a segment on its own.
vlan.formHelp: Format only: Steward checks VLAN IDs, subnets and addresses, not overlaps, and reads nothing from switches.
vlan.emptyText: Document the VLANs of this site: their subnets, ranges and who manages them.
vlan.typeHelp: What it is for: production, management, IoT, DMZ…
vlan.rulesAtHelp: A firewall and rule set, a document, a link
vlan.restrictedHelp: Access to the VLAN is restricted (an rVLAN behind a firewall).
vlan.subnetsHelp: CIDR notation, IPv4 or IPv6; ranges inside a subnet are blocked, dynamic (DHCP) or static.
vlan.subnetInvalid: Check the subnets: CIDR notation (10.20.110.0/24) and IP addresses.
vlan.segmentHelp: The Steward network segment (Catalogue → Systems) this VLAN is. Or create one from the VLAN later.
vlan.noSegments: No network segment you may see
vlan.noSegmentYet: None – create one from the VLAN (menu)
vlan.hintTitle: The VLAN and its segment differ
vlan.hintVid: VLAN ID {{vlan}} here, {{segment}} on the segment.

segment.title: Network segment from VLAN {{name}}
segment.help: Steward adds a network segment to the system catalogue with VLAN ID {{vid}} and the subnets {{subnets}}, and links it to the VLAN. Its owners, documents and firewall changes are kept there.
segment.name: Name of the segment

zone.title: Zones
zone.help: IEC 62443-3-2 zones: assets with the same security requirements. The target security level (SL-T) stays open until a risk assessment sets it.
zone.formHelp: A zone groups VLANs of this site with the same security requirements (IEC 62443-3-2).
zone.emptyText: Group the VLANs of this site into zones, and connect the zones with conduits.
zone.criticalityHelp: The consequence of a compromise of the assets in it
zone.levelHelp: Where the zone sits, bottom to top; the diagram draws the zones in this order
zone.slTargetHelp: Empty: open until a risk assessment sets it
zone.slOpenHint: No risk assessment has set the target security level yet.
zone.riskAssessmentHelp: The assessment that set SL-T: a document number or link
zone.assessmentRequired: Name the risk assessment that set SL-T.
zone.systemsHelp: Systems in this zone without a VLAN of the site – a cloud service, an enterprise system. The diagram places them here.
zone.platformsHelp: Platforms in this zone, such as an IoT platform in the external zone.
zone.hiddenItemsKept_one: {{count}} more system or platform in this zone is not visible to you; it stays as it is.
zone.hiddenItemsKept_other: {{count}} more systems or platforms in this zone are not visible to you; they stay as they are.

conduit.title: Conduits
conduit.help: IEC 62443-3-2 conduits: the connections between two zones with their protocols and controls. Firewall changes link to a conduit (Links → Conduit).
conduit.formHelp: A conduit connects two zones of this site.
conduit.protocolsHelp: With their ports: opc-ua tcp/4840, https tcp/443 (Enter after each)
conduit.controlsHelp: Firewall, data diode, jump host … (Enter after each)
conduit.needZones: A conduit connects two zones: add zones first.

device.title: Devices
device.help: The network identity of the asset: host name, MAC, VLAN, address and switch port.
device.siteHelp: The devices of every asset of this site. Add, change or remove them here or on the asset’s page.
device.formHelp: MAC addresses are EUI-48 (any usual spelling), addresses IPv4 or IPv6.
device.emptyText: Add the first one here or on the page of its {{type}}.
device.noVlans: The site has no VLAN yet
device.systemHelp: The system in the catalogue that this device is – an edge device is equipment here and a host there. The host name stays here; the system shows it.
device.systemHidden: It is linked to a system you may not see. It stays unless you choose another.
device.flagsHelp: What is ordered or done: device_ordered, port_ordered, address_ordered…

path.title: Data paths
path.help: What data leaves the asset, who collects it, how it is transferred and where it ends up. Peers and destinations are Steward items, so chains can be followed: a path continues in the paths that read from what it writes to.
path.siteHelp: The data paths of every asset of this site, with the links of their chains. Add, change or remove them here or on the asset’s page.
path.formHelp: A collector (a Steward application, platform or process, or a job elsewhere), its transfers and the destinations.
path.emptyText: Add the first one here or on the page of its {{type}}.
path.subject: Subject
path.subjectHelp: What data: machine state, NC programs, energy values…
path.noDevices: The asset has no device yet
path.hostHelp: The Steward system it runs on
path.transferIncomplete: Each transfer needs a protocol and its peer.
path.search: Search subject, collector, protocol, peer, destination
path.transfersHelp: Seen from the collector. The peer is the other end of the transfer: what the collector pulls from or receives from is where the data comes from; what it pushes to is a target, like a destination.
path.peerIsHost: This is the system the collector runs on. A service on the same host – a database, a broker – is usually a Steward system of its own: name that one, so chains and the diagram show it.

asset.title: OT network
asset.help: Its devices, data paths and live status. The live status comes only from linked checks.
asset.emptyText: This {{type}} has no devices, data paths or checks yet.

quality.title: Data quality
quality.help: What looks wrong in the documentation of the devices of this site (retired devices left out). Each device leads to its row.

kinds.duplicate_hostname_one: Host name {{value}} is used by {{count}} device
kinds.duplicate_hostname_other: Host name {{value}} is used by {{count}} devices
kinds.vlan_missing_one: {{count}} device names VLAN “{{value}}”, which this site does not have
kinds.vlan_missing_other: {{count}} devices name VLAN “{{value}}”, which this site does not have
kinds.switch_case_one: One switch written in different letter case: {{variants}}
kinds.switch_case_other: One switch written in different letter case: {{variants}}

modeHelp.pull: The collector fetches the data from the peer
modeHelp.push: The collector sends the data to the peer
modeHelp.receive: The peer sends the data to the collector (a PLC publishing over MQTT)

edge.title: Edge device
edge.help: Devices of this asset that are Steward systems: the applications that run on them and what they collect.
edge.noApps: No application is recorded as running on this system.
edge.appsHidden_one: and {{count}} application you may not see
edge.appsHidden_other: and {{count}} applications you may not see
edge.systemHidden: a system you may not see
edge.collectsHelp: Collections whose collector runs on this device – as its host, or as an application that runs on it – by the asset they read.
edge.collectsHidden_one: and {{count}} collection on an asset you may not see
edge.collectsHidden_other: and {{count}} collections on assets you may not see
edge.devicesHidden_one: and {{count}} device on a site you may not see
edge.devicesHidden_other: and {{count}} devices on sites you may not see
edge.hostNameHere: The host name, domain and address are kept on the plant device.
edge.iemNotFound: Industrial Edge device {{id}}: no status in a dataset you may see
